description: Deliberate mistakes for the steps that work in the round, sock heels and toes, each refused in plain words and changing nothing, around a few steps that work. A flat piece of 20 sts is joined into the round only at the start of a row at an edge (not partway through a row or at a short-row turn, and not twice); a flat chart is not worked in the round; short rows need a part worked flat. Needle groups must have names, distinct names and stitches, add up to the needle, and be set at the start of a round. Shaping must change something, every 1 or more rounds, on groups that exist, and reach its stitch count by whole repeats without emptying the needle or a group. Picking up needs stitches, a group when the needle has groups and a known group when named, the right side facing, an edge (not a short-row turn), and for a part worked flat, a side of it: the right side at the start of a right-side row, the left side at its end, or the right side at the end of the round after the part is joined again. Short rows at the gap need a gap ahead, room before or past it and room for their decrease. Joining a part worked flat back needs the right side facing. Closing needs no stitches resting outside a part worked flat, a whole round, and two equal halves. Sections marked flat or in the round that do not start that way are warned about, as is a part still worked flat at the end. A side of a part worked flat moves with its stitches: after picking up at the start of its right-side row the work is still at its right side (a second pick-up there is warned about), after picking up at the end of the row it is past the picked-up stitches, not at a side, and once the part is joined back in, its right side is after the stitches picked up before its first stitch. The start of the round cannot move while part of the round is worked flat, and a German turn just after a decrease that leaves a single stitch to work is refused.
covers: every refusal of join to work in the round, working flat over part of the round, rows, shaping, picking up, needle groups and closing
a flat chart in the round
an unchecked change that stops the needle groups
a part worked flat left at the end of the pattern
sides of a part worked flat that move with picked-up stitches
moving the start of the round while working flat
a German turn after a decrease

issues.message: Flat start: the section is marked as worked in the round, but the work is flat when it starts; start the section with a step that joins the work into the round, or mark it as worked flat
Flat start, step 1: works part of the stitches flat, but the work is already flat; put the other stitches on hold instead
Flat start, step 3: joins the work into the round partway through a row (15 stitches still to work in it); join at the end of a row
Flat start, step 6: joins the work into the round at a short-row turn; work to the end of the row first
Flat start, step 7: divides the stitches into groups at a short-row turn; do it at the start of a row
Flat start, step 8: works whole rows, but the work is at a short-row turn here; work to the end of the row first
Flat start, step 9: works to the gap an earlier short row left, but no stitches are waiting past a turn ahead in this row
Flat start, step 14: the work is already in the round
Flat start, step 15, chart row 1: the chart is for working flat (it has wrong-side rows), but the work is in the round here; use knit, purl or row steps for the rounds
Flat start, step 16: turns partway through a round; to work short rows over part of the round (a short-row heel), first add a step that works part of the stitches flat
Groups: the section is marked as worked flat, but the work is in the round when it starts; start the section with a step that works part of the stitches flat, or mark it as worked in the round
Groups, step 1: the groups add up to 18 stitches, but 17 are on the needle
Groups, step 2: the needle group left has 0 stitches
Groups, step 3: a needle group has no name
Groups, step 4: two needle groups are called Sole
Groups, step 6: divides the stitches into groups partway through a round (15 stitches still to work in it); do it at the start of a round
Groups, step 7: works whole rounds, but this round is already started (15 stitches still to work in it); finish the round first
Groups, step 8: closes the stitches partway through a round (15 stitches still to work in it); finish the round first
Groups, step 9: starts working flat partway through a round (15 stitches still to work in it); Ply starts a part worked flat at the start of the round
Groups, step 10: shapes over whole rounds, but this round is already started (15 stitches still to work in it); finish the round first
Groups, step 12: works 0 rounds; work at least 1
Groups, step 13: grafting joins two equal halves, but 17 stitches do not divide evenly
Groups, step 16: grafting joins two halves, but the stitches are in 3 needle groups (instep, sole, heel); divide them into two groups first
Groups, step 17: changes no stitches; to work rounds without shaping, use a step that works whole rounds
Groups, step 18: shapes every 0 rounds; give 1 to shape every round, or 2 for every other round
Groups, step 19: names the needle group instep twice
Groups, step 20: there is no needle group called gusset on the needle here
Groups, step 21: shapes 0 times; shape at least once
Groups, step 22: shapes until 16 stitches remain, but that is how many are on the needle already
Groups, step 23: decreases, but 20 stitches is more than the 16 on the needle
Groups, step 24: decreases 4 stitches at a time, which cannot reach 9 from 16: it goes from 12 to 8
Groups, step 25: takes off 20 stitches, but only 16 are on the needle
Groups, step 26: takes 5 stitches off the sole, which has only 5 stitches
Groups, step 27: the stitches are in needle groups (instep, sole, heel); say which group the picked-up stitches go on
Groups, step 28: there is no needle group called gusset; the groups are instep, sole, heel
Groups, step 29: picks up 0 stitches; pick up at least 1

Groups, step 30: this step adds stitches in its own words, so Ply cannot tell how the change falls between the needle groups (instep, sole, heel); it stops counting the groups here (divide the stitches into groups again to count them)
Groups, step 31: adds the stitches to the needle group sole, but the stitches are not divided into groups yet; divide them first, or leave the group out
Groups, step 32: shapes the needle group sole, but the stitches are not divided into groups yet; divide them first, or leave the group out
Groups, step 33: picks up along a part worked flat, but the step that worked it flat is gone (it may have been deleted)
Groups, step 34: names Flat start, step 2, which does not work stitches flat
Groups, step 35: picks up along the heel, but Groups, step 9 could not work it flat
Groups, step 36: picks up along the heel before Heel, step 1 works it; move this step after it
Groups, step 37: works 20 stitches flat, but the round has only 17 stitches
Groups, step 38: works 0 stitches flat; work at least 1
Heel, step 2: part of the round is already worked flat; join it back into the round first
Heel, step 3: divides the stitches into groups while part of the round is worked flat; divide them in the round, before working part of it flat
Heel, step 4: closes the stitches while others rest on the needle outside the part worked flat; join them back into the round first
